ai.description: The Common Krait reaches 1–1.5m. It has a glossy black body with narrow white crossbands and a distinct vertebral ridge. The head is barely wider than the neck, featuring enlarged hexagonal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Bungarus caeruleus* is the presence of enlarged, hexagonal vertebral scales along the center of its back, which are absent in lookalikes.
ai.habitat: The Common Krait inhabits diverse landscapes, including agricultural fields, scrublands, and human settlements, ranging from sea level up to 1,700 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Common Krait is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dusk to forage for snakes, lizards, and small mammals while remaining shy and reclusive during daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Common Krait is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 6–15 eggs between April and June. Females often guard their nests until the young hatch.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Common Krait is found throughout the Indian subcontinent, ranging from sea level up to 1,700 meters across diverse habitats in India, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
